event: The card confirms: Allure acquired from Colette Vane, plus 10%, 14.0 to 15.6.

changes.note: Pearl takes Colette's Allure: 10% of Colette's 16.0 added to her own 14.0

event: Pearl's sheet now reads Allure 15.6; the System states it flatly and never gloats.
The card hangs frost-bright in the corner of her eye for hours after Colette.
Since Tuesday, three people have walked into a door, a lamppost and a fountain, staring at her.
The whole room tilts toward her now, like a field of flowers when the sun moves.
A barista forgets her order halfway through and has to ask again, pink to the ears.
A woman on the tram looks at her the way you look at weather coming in.
In a dark shop window she sees the improved her, and thinks: thanks, Lettie.
She calls Colette Lettie now, a name Colette never let anyone use.
Pearl reckons them square: Colette got to stop, and she gets to keep going.
She tells the reader, still here despite her warning, that she knew she liked them.
The death is ruled a fall: a clumsy girl alone after hours, landing on something sharp.
The sweet wardrobe girl who found her and wept sits at the top of every list.
A kind detective's suspicion slides off her face; fifteen-point-six is the finest alibi.
She says she'd have done anything for Lettie, and he apologises for troubling her.
For a week flowers brown by the stage door, beside a laminated photo of Colette mid-leap.
Wearing a piece of the dead girl among the mourners, Pearl drinks their grief like sun.
Mr. Aldous finds her by the flowers.
He says she shouldn't be back here with the mops and the misery.
He looks at her as they all do now: last month too sweet to be prey, now simply too pretty.
He invites her up on Saturday, when he's having people: she'll brighten the place.
She touches his sleeve, and he forgets the sentence he was building, giving like wet paper.
On Saturday his "up" is the top of a glass tower, the whole city glittering below.
His guests have never carried their own anything; the champagne glows low warm gold.
Women lacquered to a shine, and a string quartet nobody listens to.
Pearl moves through it glowing, gathering glances like windfall apples in her skirt.
The lights drop and the ceiling opens.
A woman comes down two red silks out of the dark, forty feet into the cleared centre.
Her name is Dove; she wears almost nothing, because the body is the costume.
She climbs the air, drops, and catches herself on one arm, held level forty feet up.
Beside her strength, Pearl, Celerity 11.0, feels like a clever housecat.
There is no net or wire; Dove falls laughing and catches herself at the last breath.
Pearl wants the empty socket where Dove's fear should be, to wear as her own.
At the back with a glass of gold going warm, Pearl feels the hum start behind her eyes.
The hum is her appetite waking, and over Dove it sings richer than anything since Lettie.
She wants Dove before she has decided to, and knows by that that it is love.
With fifteen-point-six she doesn't chase; she stands in the kindest light and waits.
Robed, Dove passes through the crowd and finds her way to the one unimpressed face.
"You're not impressed," Dove says, delighted, her pulse still fluttering from the drop.
Up close Dove's beauty is colder and cleaner, a notch under Pearl's, and she wants it anyway.
Pearl says she's completely impressed and won't embarrass them both by saying so; Dove laughs.
Pearl touches her arm, feels the dense humming muscle, and holds it one beat past friendly.
As the party goes loose and loud, Dove invites her up to the rigging loft, where nobody bothers.
On the steel catwalk above the atrium, the city burning gold beyond the glass, they are alone.
Dove leans on the rail and tells how on the silks the fear leaves you a piece at a time.
Pearl feels calm and certain, a craftswoman with the right tool already in her hand.
Dove leans to point at something below, and her weight sits in exactly the wrong place.
Pearl helps her over the rail, the way she helps everyone.
Dove does not laugh as she falls; the part of her with no fear finally finds some.
The click: the loupe swings down, and Dove lies bent wrong on the gold-lit marble far below.
Dove becomes a rack of beautiful things, one of them Pearl's to take.
Leaning where Dove leaned, Pearl reads the readout with slow, greedy pleasure.
Appraisal of Dove, unpowered; Pearl: Might 8, Vit 9, Cel 11, Acu 12, Will 10, Allure 15.6.
The card says: select one, one only.
She decides Dove's flowers will be white, and that she will stand in them later.
First, up in the gold and the quiet, she has a choice to make, and means to enjoy every second.
